_comment: Goes in the TARGET repo at .pi/models.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Until 2026-09-16 the pipeline sent no sampling
parameters at all. Pi only sends them when something defines them, and
OpenRouter does not substitute a default — it omits the parameter upstream
and whichever provider serves the request applies its own. A `:free` model
routes across several providers, so the sampling that produced any given
token was chosen by whoever answered, and a retry can land somewhere else.
That is `NOTES.md` 43, and the leading candidate for the token soup in 38.
`samplingParams` is merged VERBATIM into the request body and its keys win
(`models.md`), so it carries both the sampling AND OpenRouter's top-level
`provider` routing block.
ON `require_parameters: true`. It restricts routing to providers that honour
every parameter in the request. Kept deliberately, as a decision on
2026-09-16: if we are pinning sampling at all, we want it actually applied,
and a loud failure is better than a provider quietly ignoring it. The cost
is that when NO provider qualifies, OpenRouter errors rather than falling
back — so this can take a `:free` variant from one eligible host to none.
The first review run after this file landed failed three times in three
seconds on stopReason=error, and this flag is the obvious suspect. It is
NOT established: the implementer ran fine with the same flag, and the
hypothesis that the reviewer's model lacks `tool_choice` was checked and is
WRONG — Pi does not send `tool_choice` (probed 2026-09-16, request body is
model, messages, stream, stream_options, store, max_completion_tokens,
tools). The driver now logs `errorMessage` next to `stopReason`, so the
next failure will say what it actually was rather than that it happened.
`top_p` is NOT set for laguna. OpenRouter's model list does not include
top_p in its supported_parameters at all, so sending it was wrong
regardless of routing — and with require_parameters on it would guarantee
zero eligible providers.
No `sort`. Sorting by throughput selects the fastest node, which is also how
you find a heavily quantised one — the opposite of what we are testing.
